what: 1px markers are planted throughout the page. When the top edge of the screen passes down through a ±100px band (±30px on phones) around a marker, the state of the target (usually body) changes to that marker’s value, and when it passes going up it changes to the previous marker’s value (none for the first marker). Outside the band it stays as is. When the state changes, background and text color shift over .7s and an overlay fitted to that state (a dark patterned panel etc.) turns on over .7s ease-out. This is a wedding site’s section transition, where the whole page goes dark in the dining section and turns bright again in the report section

options.band-narrow: Band (px) for windows 767px and below — if absent, band is used as is (Brand first page 30 · About page 400)
options.attr: Attribute name to hold the state, default data-tone — the consuming CSS uses [data-tone="2"Paint with ]
options.[data-fx-part=mark]: Marker (1px) — the state while data-key passes down through that marker. If absent, 1·2·3 in order
options.[data-fx-part=veil]: (If present) states listed in data-key separated by spaces ("1 2"), an overlay that turns on only then
options.--fx-dur: Background / text color duration (css variable), default .7s
options.--fx-ease: Background and text color curve (css variable), default ease
options.--fx-veil-dur · --fx-veil-ease: Cover length and curve, default --fx-dur · ease-out
